mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% over the prior month triggers a risk premium adjustment that drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed inflation spikes above 0.3%, or the effect is absent in non-inflationary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% for three consecutive months is associated with increased wage pressures that boost equity valuations and produce positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat during the identified labor cost acceleration, or the effect is not significant in regression (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in monthly RSAFS industrial production below the 50th percentile for the past 12 months signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward out-of-sample returns during demand contractions are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the signal is not predictive in expansion phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly INDPRO supply index below 90 (2017=100) coincides with reduced production capacity, triggering a negative feedback loop that drives negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive during confirmed supply shocks, or the effect is not robust across multiple contraction events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, the increased policy rate is expected to discount future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the policy tightening, or the effect is absent in non-tightening regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly UNRATE increases above 0.2% indicate strengthening labor market conditions, which are associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns through optimism about wage growth.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns during the identified labor strength, or the effect is not robust in weak labor markets.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures suggests weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 5-day forward returns as market anticipates profit compression.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative during confirmed demand weakness, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between INDPRO falling below 95 and HOUST (industrial production of goods) also falling below 110 indicates dual supply-side pressures, which increases the likelihood of negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during simultaneous supply declines in both components, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
